text:
Aisha: quick heads-up — opened a terraform PR that changes HPA target for tenant-api from 50% -> 30% because of bursty traffic. PR: https://github.com/redwood/infra/pull/4321
Ron: saw it. is this to stop 503s during bursts?
Aisha: yes, bursts + long startup causing not enough replicas. Right now HPA min=0, max=10.
Luca: hmm min=0 -> scale-to-zero could be the problem. Did you also update Karpenter provisioner TTL / scale-from-zero?
Aisha: not yet. thinking to set min=1 for tenant-api, and add provisioner annotation `karpenter.sh/scale-down-delay: "60s"`
Maya: +1 to min=1. Also check VPA — it's enabled in 'recommendation' only?
Aisha: VPA is in "recommendation" mode; not applying. PR includes note to revisit auto mode later.
devops-bot: CI passed for terraform fmt & plan :white_check_mark:
Ron: quick sanity check — will this increase cost? likely a small steady cost due to min=1. ok for prod tenant only?
Aisha: yes only prod, staging keeps min=0. I'll add a rollout note and a canary (10% traffic) to watch tail latencies.
Luca: also ensure HPA is using the right metric. If we rely on custom RPS metric instead of CPU, the HPA can react faster for request bursts.
Aisha: good point — current HPA uses `cpu` metric. I'll add `metrics { type = "Pods" ... }` to tf and wire the rps exporter.
Maya: secret wiring — if you're touching annotations or new metrics, double-check Vault path `secret/data/tenant/karpenter` was rotated last week. If TF reads the token from workspace secret, we should update that.
Aisha: noted, will verify Vault and update docs.
Ron: can we also add an annotation to the service to prefer warm nodes? maybe `node.kubernetes.io/prefer-warm: "true"` so Karpenter favours already-running instances during canary.
Luca: that annotation is non-standard but we do have a provisioner selector that respects `karpenter.k8s.aws/instance-lifecycle`. We could add a label on pods instead for the canary.
Aisha: ok i'll add pod label `scale.profile=warm` and a provisioner constraint.
Maya: small ops ask — include a note in the runbook for how to revert to min=0 and how to drain one replica safely.
Aisha: will add rollback steps and a quick `kubectl` command snippet.
Aisha: snippet I'll add to PR:
```
# set HPA min back to 0
kubectl patch hpa tenant-api -p '{"spec": {"minReplicas": 0}}' -n prod
```
Ron: lgtm, ping me after you add prod tfvars and the runbook section.
Aisha: pinging when ready. thanks! :pray:
deploy-bot: merge queued — awaiting Ron approval before apply.
